text:
maya: Heads up — got a customer (acct: acme-telemetry) hitting schema validation errors when they use streaming tool calls. They say the tool args arrive as partial JSON fragments and the downstream webhook rejects it. Ticket #INC-2026-341.

ryan: uh oh. Do we have a sample of the stream from the client?

maya: pasted below (sanitized). They used our JS SDK with streaming=true. The stream contains repeated deltas like this: 

```
data: {"type":"tool_call","name":"search_tool","arguments":"{\"query\":\"error on production\", \"filters\":[\"app:api\", \"env:prod\"], \"page\":1"}

data: {"type":"tool_call.delta","arguments":"\", \"size\":20}

data: {"type":"tool_call.delta","arguments":"}
```

maya: So you can see the arguments string is split across events; the downstream webhook tries to parse each incoming event as a full tool-call payload and fails on the partial chunk.

alex: Is the webhook our code or the customer's?

maya: customer's. They expect our runtime to send a single complete tool_call event with full arguments when the streaming sequence finishes. Instead their receiver processes every event.

ryan: Hm. Our streaming contract is that we stream incremental function_call.arguments (like OpenAI's partial function_call). Customers must reassemble. But we shouldn't break customers that treat each event as a full message.

irene: We need to know whether the SDK or the runtime is emitting an incomplete top-level event type. From the sample the type field is "tool_call" in the first event — that should indicate start-of-call. Does the QA harness show something similar? ops-bot: Attached latest runtime logs for that customer (trace id t-9c3).

support-bot: (automation) Created internal issue RINF-1538 and attached customer logs. Priority: P2.

alex: Repro checklist request: can someone post the exact curl or SDK sequence? Also which SDK version?

maya: Customer used @redwood/js v0.8.2, streaming via ws connection. Repro steps they gave: 
1) Start streaming chat with messages that prompt a function call.
2) Listen to stream and forward each payload immediately to their HTTP webhook.
3) Observe JSON parse errors on the webhook.

ryan: I can repro locally with the same SDK. Quick paste of what I see from the raw stream: 

```
{type: "tool_call", name: "search_tool", arguments: "{\"query\":\"disk space\", \"cursor\":null, \"limit\":10"
{type: "tool_call.delta", arguments: ", \"filters\":[] }"
{type: "tool_call.complete"}
```

ryan: The issue: some clients treat the first object as a complete message, parse arguments as JSON and blow up.

irene: Two axes: 1) Do we document that partial function arguments will stream and consumers must reassemble? 2) Could runtime send a clear boundary event that indicates "this is partial; wait for complete" — e.g., only emit "tool_call_complete" with full args in a final envelope?

alex: For compatibility we should do both: improve docs and add a compatibility envelope for a short window (customers expect full payloads). Implementation idea: buffer per-stream until we have tool_call_complete, then emit a single consolidated tool_call_complete event containing full arguments. Meanwhile keep current delta events for consumers that already handle streaming.

maya: Customer asked for a hotfix — they can't change their webhook quickly. Can we add a runtime switch or header that tells server to consolidate?

ryan: We can add a query param e.g., ?stream_mode=consolidated to the streaming endpoint, or honor a header X-Redwood-Stream-Mode: consolidated. Quick patch to runtime router to aggregate deltas server-side and produce one final event should be small but must be careful with memory for large args.

irene: Also add size guard: if args exceed 512KB, keep streaming (no consolidation) and return 431 or explicit 'fragmented' marker so customer knows to reassemble.

ops-bot: (log snippet) runtime/service.c: streaming_worker: assembled bytes=1789 trace=t-9c3 user=acme-telemetry.

support-bot: (automation) Noted customer escalation level: customer-reported-prod-impact. Suggested response template: "we can enable server-side consolidation for your account immediately while we work on broader fix".

maya: I already proposed that to the customer — they accepted. Can eng turn it on for acme-telemetry?

alex: I'll own the toggle. Adding per-account consolidation flag is fastest: patch config store -> toggle -> runtime picks up via feature-flags cache. I'll open a PR and patch one host. ETA 4 hours.

ryan: I'll push E2E repro that posts each intermediate event to a local webhook to validate consolidation behavior and test both modes. Tests: 
- stream_mode=streaming (behave as today)
- stream_mode=consolidated (emit single final tool_call_complete with full args)
- large payloads -> still chunked + 'fragmented' marker

irene: Also need to update docs: Developer guides > streaming tool calls: clarify semantics and show reassembly code for common runtimes (Node, Python). Add example that reconstructs arguments from incremental chunks.

maya: Customer confirmed they can accept temporary consolidation while they adjust their webhook. Please keep me posted.

alex: PR #2045 created. Will enable flag for acme-telemetry after smoke tests.

ryan: Quick note on root cause: our event envelope previously used the same top-level 'type' for start/delta pieces. That ambiguous envelope made naive receivers treat each as full. The consolidate option will emit a non-ambiguous final message: 

```
{ "type": "tool_call_complete", "name": "search_tool", "arguments": "{...full args...}" }
```

alex: rolling toggle to one runtime in staging now. ping when smoke passes.

ops-bot: (automation) Deploy to staging host staging-12 started.

ryan: smoke looks good — staging host re-emits final consolidated message and webhook receives valid JSON once per call.

alex: Enabled account flag for acme-telemetry in prod (feature-flag id ff_consolidate_streams). Monitoring for 30m.

support-bot: (automation) Noted customer notification sent.

maya: Customer confirmed resolution — no more parse errors. They asked for ETA on permanent fix / public docs.

irene: Roadmap: 1) ship final runtime fix that always emits a clear final envelope while retaining delta streaming for those who opt-in (Q2 sprint). 2) Docs update this week. 3) Add e2e tests + synthetic to catch regressions.

alex: I'll follow up with an RFC for the final envelope shape and memory safety limits.

maya: Thanks all. Closing internal incident once RFC + PR merged. :tada:
